title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In these 1986 notes Grothendieck axiomatizes 1-dimensional 'models of forms'. Such a model is a pair (L,S). L is a set of points. S is a set of 'segments'. Each segment I has a support Ĩ ⊂ L and a boundary ∂I ∈ P_2(L), a two-element subset. The structure satisfies axioms F1–F5. The previous page shows that restricting to a subset L' ⊂ L gives a model again. A special case is L' = Ĩ, whose segments are the subsegments S^I of I.

This page. A model is called a 'segment model' when some I ∈ S has Ĩ = L. That I is then unique, and L_+ = Ĩ° = L \ ∂I (the interior points).

Grothendieck now wants to recover the linear order on such a segment from the purely combinatorial data of subsegments.
- Fix an orientation: choose x_0 ∈ ∂I and let x_1 be the other endpoint.
- For a point x, let [x_0,x] = Ĩ_{x_0,x} be the support of the unique subsegment with endpoints x_0 and x. Define [x,x_1] symmetrically. Degenerate cases: [x_0,x_0] = {x_0}, [x_0,x_1] = Ĩ, and symmetrically for x_1. These are written out on the next page.
- Define x ≼ y iff y ∈ [x,x_1].
- He briefly tried, then crossed out, a variant: '… or [x_0,x] ∩ [y,x_1] = ∅ (mutually exclusive)'. That is a strict-order or trichotomy formulation.
- NB on the page: y ∈ [x,x_1] ⇔ x ∈ [x_0,y].

Transitivity. It reduces to: y ∈ [x,x_1] implies [y,x_1] ⊂ [x,x_1]. In words, a subsegment of a subsegment is a subsegment, and segments are determined by their endpoints. He calls this 'immediate'.

Proposition. The following are equivalent: (i) y ∈ [x,x_1]; (ii) [y,x_1] ⊂ [x,x_1]; (i bis) x ∈ [x_0,y]; (ii bis) [x_0,x] ⊂ [x_0,y]. The sentence breaks off.

He then starts to define C = Ĩ_{x_1,x} (or Ĩ, or {x_1} in the degenerate cases) to handle the boundary points. The next page redoes this cleanly. It concludes that ≤ is a preorder, indeed an order: [x_0,x] = [x_0,y] forces x = y.

Purpose. To show that the abstract 'segment' axiomatics F1–F5 reconstruct a totally ordered interval. In effect this identifies a segment model with a linearly ordered set with endpoints. Presumably this is a step toward classifying 1-dimensional models (segments and circles) as combinatorial or tame-topological 'forms'.
errors: Transitivity is declared 'immédiat' without citing which axiom gives the nesting [y,x_1] ⊂ [x,x_1] when y ∈ [x,x_1]. It needs uniqueness of subsegments with given endpoints and closure of S^I under taking subsegments, presumably among F1–F5. Plausible but unverified on this page.
The boundary cases x = x_0 or x = x_1 are not handled on this page. Grothendieck notices this himself (the definition of C, then the 'Notations' on the next page).
Totality of the order (any two points comparable) is not addressed here. It is needed for 'linear order' and must come from the axioms.

ideas.what: Recovering a linear order on a segment from its system of subintervals / betweenness, after choosing an orientation (endpoint x_0)
ideas.modern_name: Order from betweenness / interval structures; axiomatics of linear order via betweenness
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pasch (1882), Huntington & Kline (1917), Hilbert's order axioms; interval/convexity spaces (van de Vel)
ideas.where_published: Only in these archival notes (cote 156-1); Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame topology but not this axiomatics

ideas.what: Combinatorial axiomatics (F1–F5) of 1-dimensional 'forms' as (points, segments with supports and 2-point boundaries)
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial models of 1-dimensional tame spaces / graphs and o-minimal 1-dim cells
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight) for tame topology; graph-theoretic models classically
ideas.where_published: Programme announced vaguely in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (topologie modérée); details unpublished

missed.claim: Part of an unpublished axiomatic 'geometry of forms' in dimension 1. Here a 'segment model' is shown to carry a canonical linear order up to reversal. The program as a whole (F1–F5 axioms, models of forms) was never developed in the literature. This page itself is routine.
missed.quote: Un modèle est dit modèle-segment si ∃ I∈S tel que Ĩ = L … Je vais définir une relation d'ordre sur L
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mild historical interest: a concrete trace of Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at a purely combinatorial foundation of tame topology, parallel to o-minimality. The mathematics on this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary reconstruction of an order from interval/betweenness data, classical since Pasch/Hilbert. Its only interest is as part of the unpublished 'formes' axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: The first line most likely reads 'Un modèle est dit modèle-segment', not 'Une variété est dite variété-bisignée'.
'de préordre' / 'd'ordre': the relation is introduced as an order on L. There is an overwritten 'du/préordre'.
The definition on this page is 'x ≼ y ssi y ∈ [x,x_1]'. The crossed-out alternative is '[x_0,x] ∩ [y,x_1] = ∅' with the marginal note '(mutuellement exclusif)'.
Page number at the bottom left of the image is 10.
